threats.title: PToken.claimSurplus has no access control — attacker can claim tokens sent directly to PToken for themselves
threats.description: claimSurplus(address who) is public with no caller restriction. Any surplus tokens held by the contract (underlying balance above totalBalances) are credited to the caller-supplied `who` address. A user who sends underlying tokens to PToken without using wrap() loses those tokens to whoever calls claimSurplus first.

steps.finding: wrap() calls safeTransferFrom then claimSurplus(msg.sender) atomically — safe path
claimSurplus is public, takes arbitrary `who`, checks currBalance > totalBalances and credits surplus to `who` — any caller can supply any beneficiary
User directly transfers underlying to PToken contract; attacker front-runs by calling claimSurplus(attacker) in same or subsequent block

threats.title: Exec.deferLiquidityCheck accepts arbitrary account — attacker can freeze any account's deferLiquidityStatus to block liquidation
threats.description: deferLiquidityCheck takes an unconstrained `account` address. An attacker can set any victim account's deferLiquidityStatus to DEFERLIQUIDITY__CLEAN, occupying it for the duration of the callback, potentially blocking a concurrent liquidation that checks this flag.

dismissedCandidates.title: DToken.borrow pushes tokens before checkLiquidity (CEI violation)
dismissedCandidates.reason: The nonReentrant modifier (Base.sol:44-50) sets a global reentrancyLock at Euler storage level before pushTokens executes. Because all modules delegatecall into Euler's storage, the lock prevents any reentrant call into borrow or other nonReentrant functions during the safeTransfer. The liquidity check at line 119 fires at the end of the same transaction with no exploitable window.

dismissedCandidates.title: DToken.flashLoan allows reentrantOK functions during callback to bypass protections
dismissedCandidates.reason: During the flashLoan callback, reentrancyLock is LOCKED. Any nonReentrant function (borrow, repay, deposit, withdraw) reverts. reentrantOK functions like deferLiquidityCheck and batchDispatch are callable, but deferLiquidityCheck only defers a liquidity check and does not itself transfer assets. The require at flashLoan:163 enforces origBalance repayment, so the final balance check catches any net shortfall.
